Men were convicted in Miami federal court for plotting to kill Jovenel Moise at his Port-au-Prince home in 2021 Four south Florida men were convicted on Friday of plotting to kill Haitian president Jovenel Moise in 2021 by hiring mercenaries to assassinate him at his Port-au-Prince home, court records show. Prosecutors argued during the nine-week trial in a Miami federal court that the men assembled two dozen former Colombian soldiers and supplied them with money, guns, ammunition and tactical vests in a conspiracy to kill Moise. The 53-year-old president was shot dead in July 2021 at his private residence in the hills above Port-au-Prince, a killing that left a gaping political vacuum in the Caribbean nation and emboldened powerful gangs.

The assassins were allegedly provided with money, firearms, ammunition and tactical gear as part of the conspiracy to kill Moïse at his private residence in Port-au-Prince in July 2021. Four South Florida men have been convicted by a United States federal court over their roles in the 2021 assassination of former Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. According to reports by CBS News and other U.S. media outlets, the men were found guilty on Friday after a nine-week trial in a federal court in Miami. Reuters reported that the prosecutors told the court that the defendants organised and financed a group of about two dozen former Colombian soldiers who travelled to Haiti as mercenaries to carry out the operation.

The jury in the trial against four men accused of conspiring to kill Haitian President Jovenel Moïse found them guilty on Friday. Moïse was assassinated inside his bedroom in 2021. His wife, Martine Moïse, was nearby and was also shot multiple times. On trial together were Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, and James Solages and all of the men now face life in prison at their sentencing. The men were never accused of the actual assassination, but rather putting the plot together that led to the killing and did so here in South Florida. The men faced four separate conspiracy charges, including one that claimed their actions led directly to the murder.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Men were convicted in Miami federal court for plotting to kill Jovenel Moise at his Port-au-Prince home in 2021

Four south Florida men were convicted on Friday of plotting to kill Haitian president Jovenel Moise in 2021 by hiring mercenaries to assassinate him at his Port-au-Prince home, court records show.

Prosecutors argued during the nine-week trial in a Miami federal court that the men assembled two dozen former Colombian soldiers and supplied them with money, guns, ammunition and tactical vests in a conspiracy to kill Moise. The 53-year-old president was shot dead in July 2021 at his private residence in the hills above Port-au-Prince, a killing that left a gaping political vacuum in the Caribbean nation and emboldened powerful gangs.

Standing trial were Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, 53, a former FBI informant, Colombian national and permanent US resident; Antonio Intriago, 62, a Venezuelan-American owner of a security firm; James Solages, 40, a Haitian-American handyman; and Walter Veintemilla, 57, an Ecuadorian American.

They were convicted of multiple counts of conspiracy to kill and kidnap a person outside the US resulting in death – and of providing material support or resources to carry out a violation resulting in death.

A fifth defendant, Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a Haitian-born doctor – who court papers say wanted to be named president after Moise was killed – will be tried later due to health issues.

The killing has prompted multiple investigations and indictments in Haiti and the United States while giving rise to competing theories over who ordered the assassination and why.

Defense lawyers for the Florida men said the government used unreliable evidence from Haiti, the Miami Herald reported. They argued their clients only intended to serve an arrest warrant on the president because he had overstayed his term.

The defendants also claimed that by the time the Colombians arrived to arrest him, Moise had already been killed by his own security forces and officials in his government.

“This is a Haitian plot and it is a Haitian conspiracy,” defense attorney Emmanuel Perez said, arguing that the men were being used as scapegoats in a flawed FBI investigation, the Miami Herald reported.

A divisive figure in Haiti who declined to leave office after his term ended in February 2021, Moise’s death added to the Caribbean nation’s political instability and unleashed widespread gang violence.

[Lähde: CBS News]
The jury in the trial against four men accused of conspiring to kill Haitian President Jovenel Moïse found them guilty on Friday.

Moïse was assassinated inside his bedroom in 2021. His wife, Martine Moïse, was nearby and was also shot multiple times.

On trial together were Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, and James Solages and all of the men now face life in prison at their sentencing.

The men were never accused of the actual assassination, but rather putting the plot together that led to the killing and did so here in South Florida.

The men faced four separate conspiracy charges, including one that claimed their actions led directly to the murder.

One of the men, Antonio Intriago, never even traveled to Haiti. But he's the owner of the Doral company the prosecutors said transported weapons, ammunition and bulletproof vests that was part of the conspiracy.

After the verdict was announced, attorneys said the fight was not over.

"We thought the government's case was insufficient," attorney David Howard said. "But we have to respect the system and respect the verdict. We're going to appeal."

The sentencing for the men is expected sometime later this summer, maybe in August or September.

In total, 13 men were arrested in connection with the assassination. Eight took plea deals, and one more man is still awaiting trial.

Moïse was assassinated on July 7, 2021, when approximately two dozen foreign mercenaries, who were mostly from Colombia, launched an attack on his home in Petionville, near Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince, according to officials.

Moïse's wife, Martine, was also seriously injured in the attack and provided dramatic and sometimes graphic testimony during the trial.

During the testimony, she said she had went to bed around 10 p.m. on July 6 while her husband was awake and working. Just after 1 a.m. on July 7, she said she woke up to the sound of gunfire.

"I was afraid," she said. "I was shocked. I never heard so many gunshots."

She said that her husband was also awakened and said to her "Honey, we are dead."

She said she dropped to her hands and knees and began to crawl on the floor to check on their children while trying to avoid being shot.

She eventually found her children and told them to hide in a bathroom while she went back to be with her husband.

payload.title: Neljä miestä tuomittiin Haitin presidentin murhaan johtaneesta salaliitosta Yhdysvalloissa
payload.summary: Miamin liittovaltion oikeudessa valamiehistö katsoi neljän Etelä-Floridan miehen syyllistyneen salaliittoon, joka johti Haitin presidentin Jovenel Moïsen surmaan vuonna 2021.
payload.content:
Neljä Etelä-Floridassa asunutta miestä on todettu syyllisiksi salaliittoon, jonka tarkoituksena oli surmata Haitin presidentti Jovenel Moïse hänen kodissaan Port-au-Princessä vuonna 2021. Tuomio annettiin perjantaina Miamin liittovaltion oikeudessa yhdeksän viikkoa kestäneen oikeudenkäynnin jälkeen, jossa käsiteltiin hyökkäyksen valmistelua ja rahoitusta.

## Syyttäjien mukaan ryhmä kokosi palkkasotilaita

Syyttäjien mukaan miehet organisoivat ja rahoittivat operaatiota, jossa noin kaksi tusinaa entistä kolumbialaissotilasta matkusti Haitiin palkkasotilaina. Oikeudessa esitetyn syyttäjän näkemyksen mukaan ryhmälle toimitettiin rahaa, ampuma-aseita, ammuksia ja taktisia varusteita, jotta suunnitelma voitiin toteuttaa Moïsen yksityisasunnossa Port-au-Princessä.

Oikeudessa tuomitut miehet ovat Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla ja James Solages. Heitä ei syytetty siitä, että he olisivat itse ampuneet Moïsen, vaan siitä, että he kokosivat murhaan johtaneen juonen ja mahdollistivat sen Etelä-Floridasta käsin. Miehet kohtasivat neljä erillistä salaliittosyytettä, joista yhdessä väitettiin heidän toimintansa johtaneen suoraan murhaan.

Miehet joutuvat myöhemmin kuulemaan rangaistuksensa. Lähdeaineiston mukaan heitä voi odottaa elinkautinen vankeusrangaistus.

## Murha syvensi Haitin poliittista kriisiä

Jovenel Moïse surmattiin heinäkuussa 2021 yksityisasunnossaan Port-au-Princen yläpuolisilla rinteillä. Hän oli kuollessaan 53-vuotias. CBS:n lähdeaineiston mukaan Moïse ammuttiin makuuhuoneessaan, ja hänen vaimonsa Martine Moïse oli lähellä hyökkäyksen aikana. Hän haavoittui useista laukauksista.

Presidentin murha jätti Haitiin syvän poliittisen tyhjiön. Lähdeaineiston mukaan surma myös rohkaisi maan voimakkaita jengejä ja pahensi jo valmiiksi vaikeaa turvallisuus- ja valtakriisiä.

Miamin oikeudenkäynti oli osa Yhdysvalloissa käsiteltyä rikoskokonaisuutta, jossa on selvitetty, miten Haitin presidentin murhaan johtanut suunnitelma valmisteltiin, rahoitettiin ja varustettiin. Perjantain tuomio kohdistui neljään mieheen, joiden katsottiin osallistuneen salaliittoon ennen varsinaista hyökkäystä.

Syyttäjien mukaan he organisoivat ja rahoittivat palkkasotilaiden ryhmää, joka liittyi Jovenel Moïsen murhaan.
